q: Dropbox 设计题的核心功能需求包括哪些？（多选）
options: 从任意设备上传文件
从任意设备下载文件
分享文件并查看别人分享给自己的文件
自动跨设备同步文件
options_en: Upload a file from any device
Download a file from any device
Share a file and view files others have shared with you
Automatically sync files across devices
why: 这题覆盖上传、下载、分享和同步四条用户主路径；编辑文件和免下载预览属于范围外。
why_en: The core Dropbox requirements are upload, download, sharing, and automatic cross-device sync.
q_en: Which core functional requirements are in the Dropbox design? (Select all that apply)
optionExplanations: 如果做不到从任意设备上传，用户只能困在装了客户端的那台机器上传文件，跨设备协作无从谈起。
下载权限缺了这条，用户换个设备就拿不到自己的文件，“随处访问”的承诺就落空。
分享和查看别人分享的文件是协作场景的核心，没有它 Dropbox 只是个人网盘，做不成团队工具。
自动跨设备同步区别于纯粹的手动上传下载——没有它，用户得自己记得去同步，体验退化成传统网盘。
optionExplanations_en: Without upload from any device, a user is stuck uploading only from the one machine with the client installed, killing multi-device use.
Without download from any device, switching devices means losing access to your own files — the 'access anywhere' promise breaks.
Sharing and viewing what's shared with you is what turns this from a personal drive into a collaboration tool.
Automatic sync is what separates this from manual upload/download — without it, users have to remember to sync themselves.
scenario: 45 分钟的 Dropbox 面试，只画跨设备存取与协作的主路径，在线编辑和预览留到最后再谈。
scenario_en: In a 45-minute Dropbox interview you only draw the cross-device access and collaboration paths; in-app editing and preview come last.

q: Dropbox 设计题里，以下哪些被明确列为 below the line（范围外）？（多选）
options: 文件编辑
无需下载即可预览文件
每用户存储上限
病毒/恶意软件扫描
options_en: File editing
Previewing files without downloading them
A per-user storage limit
Virus / malware scanning
why: 这些是真实产品能力，但不是本设计主线；范围收紧后重点转向大文件传输、同步和可靠性。
why_en: Editing, previewing without download, storage limits, and malware scanning are out of scope for this design.
q_en: Which capabilities are below the line for this Dropbox design? (Select all that apply)
optionExplanations: 文件编辑要动到内容本身和多人协作合并逻辑，是完全独立的一套系统，这道题先不展开。
免下载预览需要额外的转码/渲染服务，属于锦上添花，不影响核心的存储和同步链路。
每用户存储上限是产品计费策略问题，不影响文件怎么存、怎么传，可以后置。
病毒扫描是安全增强项，加在上传管线的某一环即可，不改变整体架构，所以先放到范围外。
optionExplanations_en: Editing touches content itself and multi-user merge logic — a whole separate system, not needed for this pass.
Rendering a preview before the file downloads needs its own transcoding/rendering service; a nice-to-have that doesn't touch core storage or sync.
A per-user storage cap is a billing/product policy question, not something that changes how files are stored or transferred.
Scanning uploads for malware is a security add-on that can slot into the pipeline later without reshaping the core architecture.
scenario: 同一场 45 分钟面试：时间只够设计大文件传输、同步和可靠性，其余能力先划到线下。
scenario_en: Same 45-minute interview: there is only time for large-file transfer, sync, and reliability, so everything else gets pushed below the line.

q: Dropbox 的核心非功能需求包括哪些？（多选）
options: 高可用，优先 availability over consistency
支持超大文件（数百 GB 到 TB 级）
安全可靠，文件丢失或损坏后可恢复
上传、下载、同步尽量低延迟
options_en: High availability, favoring availability over strict consistency
Support very large files, from hundreds of GB up to TB scale
Be secure and reliable, recovering files if they are lost or corrupted
Keep upload, download, and sync latency as low as possible
why: 文件系统能接受几秒同步延迟，但不能频繁不可用或丢文件；大文件量级直接驱动分块和续传设计。
why_en: Dropbox prioritizes high availability, very large file support, reliability, and low latency.
q_en: Which non-functional requirements matter most for Dropbox? (Select all that apply)
optionExplanations: 高可用换来的代价是接受短暂的跨区域旧值——用户能接受多等几秒看到新文件，但不能接受服务打不开。
大文件支持直接决定了要不要做分块上传和断点续传，这条约束贯穿整个设计。
文件丢失或损坏是网盘最不能犯的错，可靠性要求直接推动多副本存储和校验机制。
低延迟决定了用户体验——上传下载卡顿会让产品显得不专业，即使数据最终正确。
optionExplanations_en: Favoring uptime trades off strict freshness — users tolerate a few seconds of delay before seeing a new file, but not downtime.
Large-file support is what forces the chunking and resumable-upload design later in the interview.
Losing or corrupting a file is the one thing a storage product can't do, which drives replication and checksums.
Low latency shapes the felt experience — sluggish upload/download makes the product feel broken even when data is correct.
scenario: Dropbox 要托管数百 GB 到 TB 级文件、跨设备同步，几秒延迟可接受，但文件绝不能丢。
scenario_en: Dropbox must hold files from hundreds of GB up to terabytes and sync them across devices; a few seconds of lag is fine, losing a file is not.

scenario: 面试给出设计假设：Dropbox 系统要支持单个文件最大 50GB。
q: 这个 50GB 假设主要决定了哪个设计判断？
options: 这意味着要给 users 表和 files 表重新建索引
文件已经很大，索性放弃所有缓存层
下载可以完全交给数据库处理，不必接入 CDN
单次 POST 不现实，必须做客户端分块和断点续传
options_en: This means the users and files tables need new indexes.
The file is already large, so drop every cache layer entirely.
Downloads can be handled entirely by the database, no CDN needed.
A single POST isn't realistic; the client must chunk and support resumable upload.
why: 50GB 远超单请求的超时和请求体限制，这个量级直接把设计推向客户端分块、进度展示和断点续传。
why_en: A 50GB file makes single-request upload impractical, forcing client-side chunking, progress tracking, and resumable uploads.
q_en: What design decision does the 50GB file-size assumption force?
scenario_en: The interview assumption is that Dropbox must support a maximum single-file size of 50GB.
optionExplanations: 50GB 只是文件体积，跟 users/files 表要不要建索引是两回事，这个推论跑偏了主题。
文件大不等于放弃缓存——metadata 和小文件仍然受益于缓存，只是大文件字节走别的路径。
CDN 恰恰是加速这类大文件下载最直接的手段，跳过它反而是反方向。
这才是 50GB 直接逼出来的判断——单次请求扛不住这个体量。
optionExplanations_en: 50GB is just file size — unrelated to whether the users/files tables need new indexes; a non sequitur.
A large file doesn't mean dropping caching altogether — metadata and small files still benefit even if big bytes take a different path.
A CDN is exactly the tool for speeding up large downloads, so skipping it points the wrong direction.
This is the one conclusion the 50GB number actually forces — a single request just can't carry that much.

q: 为什么 Dropbox 通常优先可用性而不是强一致？
options: 用户能接受另一地区几秒后才看到新文件
文件系统不需要任何安全机制
Blob Storage 无法跨区域复制
强一致性反而会让下载更快
options_en: Users can accept seeing a file uploaded elsewhere only a few seconds later.
A file system does not need any security controls.
Blob storage cannot replicate across regions.
Strong consistency actually makes downloads faster.
why: 文件同步允许几秒级延迟，不必像交易系统那样保证全局强一致读到最新写。
why_en: File sync can tolerate a few seconds of delay, unlike transactional systems that must guarantee every read sees the latest write.
tradeoff: 可用性优先（容忍短暂延迟） vs 强一致（每次读最新写）
q_en: Why does Dropbox usually favor availability over strong consistency?
optionExplanations: 这就是可用性优先要付的代价——用户能接受另一地区晚几秒才看到新文件。
安全机制和一致性模型是两条正交的轴，该加密、该做权限控制跟选可用性还是强一致没关系。
Blob Storage 恰恰擅长跨区域复制，这不是它的短板。
强一致往往要等多副本写入确认，会拖慢而不是加快下载。
optionExplanations_en: This is exactly the cost of favoring availability — users accept seeing a file several seconds behind in another region.
Security and the consistency model are orthogonal — a file system still needs encryption and access control no matter which one you pick.
Blob storage is actually good at cross-region replication; that's not a real limitation.
Strong consistency usually waits on replica acknowledgments, which slows downloads down, not up.
scenario: Dropbox 同步：北美用户传完文件，欧洲同事几秒后才看到没问题，但网盘不能打不开。
scenario_en: For Dropbox sync, a teammate in Europe seeing a newly uploaded file a few seconds late is fine, but the drive being unavailable is not.

q: 补全 Dropbox 的核心实体：
text: 核心实体包括 {{File}}（原始字节）、{{FileMetadata}}（name/size/mimeType/uploadedBy 等元数据）、{{User}}（系统用户）。
why: 原始文件和元数据必须分开思考：前者走 Blob Storage/CDN 大对象路径，后者走数据库和权限查询。
why_en: The core entities are File bytes, FileMetadata, and User, because bytes and metadata follow different storage paths.

termDefinitions.meaning: 专门存储大二进制对象（如文件、图片）的存储服务，例如 S3。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Blob storage is a service for storing large binary objects such as files, for example S3.

q_en: Fill in the core Dropbox entities.

q: Dropbox 初版 API 需要覆盖哪些接口？（多选）
options: POST /files 上传文件和 metadata
GET /files/{fileId} 下载文件和 metadata
POST /files/{fileId}/share 分享给用户
GET /files/changes?since={timestamp} 查询同步变化
options_en: POST /files uploads a file and its metadata
GET /files/{fileId} downloads a file and its metadata
POST /files/{fileId}/share shares the file with other users
GET /files/changes?since={timestamp} polls for sync changes
why: 这些接口对应上传、下载、分享和同步四个功能需求；上传/下载 API 之后会演进为 signed URL 流程。
why_en: The initial API covers upload, download, sharing, and change polling for sync.
q_en: Which endpoints should the first Dropbox API cover? (Select all that apply)
optionExplanations: 上传接口是整个系统的入口——没有它文件根本进不了系统，后面的下载分享都无从谈起。
下载接口直接对应用户能不能拿回自己的文件，是最基础的读路径。
分享接口把单人存储变成协作场景，是把网盘升级成协作工具的关键一环。
变化查询接口是同步机制的基础——没有它，客户端不知道该拉取哪些远端更新。
optionExplanations_en: The upload endpoint is the entry point for the whole system — without it, nothing gets into storage for download or sharing to build on.
The download endpoint is the basic read path — it's literally whether a user can get their file back.
The share endpoint is what turns single-user storage into a collaboration feature.
The changes-polling endpoint is the backbone of sync — without it, a client has no way to know what remote updates to pull.
scenario: Dropbox 第一版 API 只服务上传、下载、分享、跨设备同步这四条功能需求，先不谈优化。
scenario_en: The first cut of the Dropbox API only has to serve four functional requirements: upload, download, share, and cross-device sync.

q: 为什么请求体里不应让客户端直接传 user 信息作为授权依据？
options: HTTP 请求体这种格式没办法装下 JSON 数据
客户端内容可伪造，身份应来自 session/JWT
上传时文件名字符会变得越来越长
这个云存储 S3 完全不支持保存任何 metadata 字段
options_en: An HTTP request body cannot hold JSON data.
Client-supplied content can be forged; identity should come from a session or JWT.
File name characters would grow longer over time.
This cloud storage, S3, does not support saving metadata fields.
why: 用户身份要来自可信认证上下文（session/JWT），请求体内容客户端可随意伪造。
why_en: User identity should come from a trusted auth context like a session or JWT, not from a forgeable request body.

termDefinitions.meaning: JSON Web Token，一种自包含、可验证签名的身份令牌。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A JWT is a self-contained, signed token used to represent an authenticated identity.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务端签发、代表已登录用户身份的凭证。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A session token is a credential issued by the server that represents a logged-in user's identity.

q_en: Why should the request body not be trusted for user identity?
optionExplanations: HTTP 请求体完全能装 JSON，这个说法本身就站不住脚。
关键在于信任边界——客户端传的任何字段都能被篡改，身份得来自服务端签发的凭证。
文件名长度跟这道题要判断的授权来源完全是两码事。
这个云存储 S3 存不存 metadata 字段跟要不要信任客户端传的身份信息毫无关系。
optionExplanations_en: An HTTP body can absolutely carry JSON — that claim doesn't hold up.
The real issue is trust boundary — any field the client sends can be forged, so identity must come from a server-issued credential instead.
File name length has no bearing on how the server determines identity.
Whether S3 stores metadata fields is unrelated to whether the request payload can be trusted for identity.
scenario: Dropbox 上传接口收到一个请求体里自带 userId 的 POST /files，服务端要据此判断谁能写。
scenario_en: The Dropbox upload endpoint gets a POST /files whose body carries its own userId, and the server has to decide from that who may write.

scenario: 文件 metadata 结构简单、关系少，主要查询模式是按用户列出文件和根据 fileId 做权限检查。
q: 默认最适合选哪类存储？
options: 把 metadata 全存进 S3 object body 里
浏览器 localStorage
DynamoDB 这类 NoSQL metadata DB
Elasticsearch 作为唯一真相
options_en: Store metadata only inside the S3 object body.
Browser localStorage.
DynamoDB, a managed NoSQL store.
Elasticsearch as the single source of truth.
why: 简单 document、按 user 查询的场景下，NoSQL 如 DynamoDB 是顺手默认；SQL 数据库同样可行。
why_en: For simple documents queried mainly by user, a NoSQL store like DynamoDB is a sensible default, though a relational database works too.
whenOtherWins: 共享关系和事务查询变复杂时，Postgres 等关系型数据库同样合理。
tradeoff: 简单文档快速上手 vs 关系型数据库的事务与复杂查询能力

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 提供的全托管 NoSQL 数据库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DynamoDB is a fully managed NoSQL database service from AWS.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向全文检索和聚合分析的搜索引擎。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Elasticsearch is a search engine built for full-text search and analytics.

q_en: Which storage type is the best default for Dropbox metadata?
scenario_en: File metadata is simple, has few relationships, and is mainly queried by user or by fileId for permission checks.
optionExplanations: 把 metadata 全部塞进 S3 object body，意味着每次查询都要下载整个对象才能读字段，完全没法索引。
localStorage 是浏览器本地存储，只服务当前设备的当前用户，撑不起服务端要处理的多设备查询。
结构简单、主要按 user 查询时，DynamoDB 这类 NoSQL 能直接按 key 查，上手快、扩展省心。
Elasticsearch 的强项是全文检索和聚合分析，把它当唯一真相来源会牺牲事务性和一致性保证。
optionExplanations_en: Putting metadata inside the S3 object body means every query has to fetch the whole object just to read a field — no indexing at all.
localStorage lives in one browser on one device; it can't serve the multi-device queries a backend needs to answer.
When the schema is simple and most lookups are scoped to one user, a managed NoSQL database such as DynamoDB gives fast key lookups with easy scaling.
Elasticsearch is built for full-text search and aggregation — using it as the source of truth gives up transactional guarantees.

scenario: 用户文件可能很多很大，应用服务器本地磁盘无法可靠、弹性地保存所有原始字节。
q: 原始文件内容应该存在哪里？
options: File Service 本地文件系统
Metadata DB 的一列
Redis Pub/Sub
S3 / GCS 这类 Blob Storage
options_en: The File Service's local file system.
A column in the metadata database.
Redis Pub/Sub.
Blob storage such as S3 or GCS.
why: 大对象需要弹性扩展和可靠性，Blob Storage 专为此设计；应用服务器本地磁盘扛不住容量和可靠性要求。
why_en: Large file bytes need elastic, reliable storage, which is exactly what blob storage like S3 provides.
whenOtherWins: 极小原型可以先用本地磁盘；生产级大文件和多设备访问才需要托管对象存储。
tradeoff: 托管对象存储的弹性与可靠性 vs 本地磁盘的简单实现

termDefinitions.meaning: Amazon 和 Google 提供的对象存储服务，用于保存大文件字节。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: S3 and GCS are cloud object storage services used to hold large file bytes.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 提供的发布订阅消息机制，不做持久化对象存储。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis Pub/Sub is a publish-subscribe messaging mechanism, not persistent object storage.

q_en: Where should the raw file bytes live?
scenario_en: Users can store many large files, and local disks on app servers cannot hold all raw bytes reliably or elastically.
optionExplanations: 本地文件系统跟着单台机器走，机器一宕机或要扩容，文件就跟着没了或拆不动。
把大字节塞进数据库列，哪怕只查文件名也要驮着几十 GB 的负载，拖垮整个查询层。
Redis Pub/Sub 是消息广播通道，消息不落盘、不持久化，根本不是用来存文件的。
大文件需要弹性容量和持久性，这正是 S3/GCS 这类对象存储从设计之初就要解决的问题。
optionExplanations_en: Local disk is tied to one machine — if it dies or you need to scale out, the files go with it or can't move.
Stuffing large bytes into a database column means every query, even one that only needs the file name, drags along tens of GB.
Redis Pub/Sub is a broadcast channel — messages aren't persisted, so it was never meant to hold files.
Large files need scalable, durable capacity, exactly the problem an object store such as S3/GCS was built to solve.

q: 客户端先上传到 File Service，再由 File Service 上传到 S3 的主要问题是什么？
options: 文件穿后端两次，又慢又贵，还压垮应用服务器
这个云存储 S3 拒绝接收后端发起的上传
metadata 记录这时候没法正常保存
用户看不到自己上传文件的名字
options_en: The file crosses the backend twice, which is slow, costly, and overloads app servers.
This cloud storage, S3, refuses uploads issued from a backend.
The metadata record cannot be saved properly at this point.
Users cannot see the name of the file they uploaded.
why: 客户端到后端、后端再到 S3，等于传两遍大文件；应用服务器还要扛大对象流量成为瓶颈。
why_en: Routing through the backend sends the file twice and turns application servers into a large-object bottleneck.
q_en: What is the main problem with proxying uploads through the File Service?
optionExplanations: 问题就在双跳传输——先到 File Service 再到 S3，同一份大文件走了两遍网络，还占满应用服务器的连接。
S3 完全接受来自服务端的上传请求，这不是它拒绝的场景。
metadata 的保存跟字节走哪条路径是两件独立的事，不会因为代理上传就存不进去。
文件名是 metadata 里的一个字段，跟传输路径无关，用户照样能看到。
optionExplanations_en: The problem is the double hop — client to backend, then backend to S3 sends the same large file across the network twice and saturates app-server connections.
S3 fully accepts uploads issued from a backend; that's not what breaks here.
Saving metadata is independent of which path the bytes take — proxying doesn't stop it from being saved.
The file name is just a metadata field, unrelated to the transfer path — users still see it fine.
scenario: Dropbox 用户上传 50GB 视频，File Service 跑在按出入流量计费的应用服务器上。
scenario_en: A Dropbox user uploads a 50GB video while the File Service runs on app servers billed by bandwidth in and out.

scenario: 要让客户端绕过应用服务器直接上传到 S3，同时仍限制只能上传到授权位置和对象。
q: 最合适的机制是什么？
options: 把 AWS root key 发给客户端
预签名上传 URL
让用户手动登录 S3 控制台
把文件先 base64 放进 JSON body
options_en: Send the AWS root key to the client.
A presigned upload URL.
Have the user log into the S3 console manually.
Base64-encode the file into a JSON body.
why: File Service 用自己的云凭证本地签一个限时限路径的 URL，客户端直接 PUT 到 S3，后端不进数据路径。
why_en: The File Service signs a time-limited, path-scoped URL with its own credentials, so the client can PUT directly to S3 without the backend touching the bytes.
whenOtherWins: 内部管理工具或很小文件可以直接走后端上传；面向用户的大文件路径应绕开后端。
tradeoff: 客户端直传的速度与解耦 vs 后端代理上传的集中控制

termDefinitions.meaning: 由服务端用云凭证签名、限时限路径的 URL，持有者可直接对该对象操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A presigned URL is a time-limited, path-scoped URL signed by the server that lets the holder access that specific object directly.

q_en: What mechanism lets clients upload directly to S3 safely?
scenario_en: Clients should bypass app servers and upload directly to S3, while still being limited to an authorized object path.
optionExplanations: 把 root key 发给客户端等于把整个云账户的钥匙交出去，一旦泄露攻击者能为所欲为。
既要客户端直传又要限制范围时，预签名 URL 刚好卡在中间——限时限路径，客户端拿到就能直接 PUT。
让用户手动登录 S3 控制台没法自动化，也完全破坏产品的上传体验。
50GB 文件 base64 编码后体积更大，还得塞进 JSON body，会直接撞穿几乎所有请求体大小限制。
optionExplanations_en: Handing the client the root key hands over the entire cloud account — one leak and an attacker can do anything.
When clients need to upload directly but stay scoped, a presigned URL sits right in the middle — short-lived and path-restricted, no long-lived credential exposed.
Making users log into the S3 console manually can't be automated and wrecks the upload experience.
Base64-encoding a 50GB file only makes it bigger, and stuffing it into a JSON body blows past nearly every request-size limit.

q: 把普通 direct-to-S3 上传流程排成正确顺序：

File Service 生成 presigned URL 并把 metadata 标记为 uploading
客户端请求 POST /files/presigned-url 并提交 metadata
S3 通知后端文件已上传
后端把 metadata 状态更新为 uploaded
why: 控制面先建 metadata 和签名 URL，数据面直传 S3；对象到位后再把状态从 uploading 推进到 uploaded。
why_en: The control plane creates metadata and a signed URL first, the client uploads bytes straight to S3, then the backend marks metadata uploaded.
diagram:
flowchart LR
Client[Client] -->|init upload| FileSvc[File Service]
FileSvc -->|signed URL| Client
Client -->|PUT bytes| Blob[(Blob Storage)]
Client -->|complete| FileSvc
FileSvc --> Meta[(Metadata DB)]

termDefinitions.meaning: 由服务端用云凭证签名、限时限路径的 URL，持有者可直接对该对象操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A presigned URL is a time-limited, path-scoped URL signed by the server that lets the holder access that specific object directly.

q_en: Put the direct-to-S3 upload flow in the right order.

scenario: 上传 API 已从单个 POST /files 演进为先申请上传权限，再把字节直传对象存储。
q: 第一步 control-plane API 应该是什么？
options: GET /files/{fileId}/bytes -> all bytes through backend
DELETE /users/me
POST /files/presigned-url -> PresignedUrl
POST /files/search
options_en: GET /files/{fileId}/bytes streams all bytes through the backend.
DELETE /users/me.
POST /files/presigned-url returns a PresignedUrl.
POST /files/search.
why: 这个接口只处理 metadata、鉴权和签名，不接收文件字节，把应用服务器留在控制面。
why_en: This endpoint only handles metadata, authorization, and signing, keeping large bytes off the application server.
whenOtherWins: 文件很小且赶工期时，单个 POST 上传可以先用；生产级大文件路径必须拆开。
tradeoff: 控制面/数据面分离 vs 单接口实现简单
q_en: What should the first control-plane upload API be?
scenario_en: The upload API has evolved from one POST /files call into requesting upload permission first, then sending bytes to object storage.
optionExplanations: GET 全量字节走后端正是要绕开的老路径，字节应该走 S3 直传。
删除用户账号跟上传流程完全不搭边，选项本身就跑题了。
第一步只需要处理鉴权和签名，字节完全不经过这个接口，应用服务器留在控制面上。
搜索接口是后续功能，不属于最初这版上传 API 要解决的问题。
optionExplanations_en: GET-ing all the bytes through the backend is exactly the old path this design avoids — bytes should go straight to S3.
Deleting a user account has nothing to do with the upload flow; the option is simply off-topic.
The first step only needs to handle auth checks and URL signing — no bytes touch this endpoint, keeping the app server on the control plane.
A search endpoint is a later feature, not something the initial upload API needs to solve.

q: 使用 Blob Storage 后，metadata 和 file bytes 之间会出现什么一致性问题？
options: 这个云存储 S3 会自动帮你创建用户账号
上传后文件名字段直接就无法保存
CDN 边缘节点会把数据库整个删掉
文件传上去了但 metadata 没存，或者反过来
options_en: This cloud storage, S3, automatically creates a user account for you.
The file name field simply cannot be saved after upload.
A CDN edge node deletes the entire database.
The file uploaded but metadata wasn't saved, or the reverse happened.
why: 大对象和元数据分处两个系统，没有单一事务；需要 status 字段和补偿清理来处理中间态。
why_en: Blob bytes and metadata live in two separate systems with no single transaction, creating partial-success states that need a status field and cleanup.
q_en: What consistency problem appears when metadata and file bytes live separately?
optionExplanations: S3 不会替你创建用户账号，这个说法跟场景完全不搭。
文件名字段的保存跟这里讨论的一致性问题无关，完全能正常写入。
CDN 边缘节点不会碰数据库，这个后果在真实系统里不会发生。
两个系统各自独立成功或失败，就会留下“字节到了但记录没写”或反过来的中间态。
optionExplanations_en: S3 doesn't create user accounts for you — that claim doesn't fit the scenario at all.
Saving the file name field is unrelated to this consistency problem; it saves fine.
A CDN edge node never touches the database — this outcome couldn't happen in a real system.
Each system can succeed or fail on its own, so you end up with bytes present but no record, or the reverse.
scenario: Dropbox 把文件字节写进 S3、元数据写进 Metadata DB，这两次写没有共同事务包住。
scenario_en: Dropbox writes the file bytes to S3 and the metadata to a separate database, and no single transaction wraps both writes.

scenario: 用户下载大文件；如果后端先从 S3 下载再转发给用户，会形成双重下载和后端瓶颈。
q: 更好的下载路径是什么？
options: 鉴权后签发 presigned URL，交给客户端直传
所有下载请求都必须先经过后端服务器代理转发
把文件字节直接复制进 Metadata DB 的一列
要求终端用户自己安装一个数据库客户端软件
options_en: Authorize, then issue a presigned URL for the client to use directly.
Every download request must first be proxied through the backend server.
Copy the file bytes directly into a column of the metadata database.
Require end users to install a database client program themselves.
why: 后端只做鉴权和签 URL，数据面由对象存储直接服务，减少带宽、延迟和应用服务器负载。
why_en: The backend only authorizes and signs the URL; object storage serves the bytes directly, cutting bandwidth, latency, and app server load.
whenOtherWins: 需要在线转码、逐字节审计或文件很小时，后端代理仍可以接受。
tradeoff: 直传省后端带宽 vs 后端代理的集中控制/审计
q_en: What is the better download path for large Dropbox files?
scenario_en: A user downloads a large file; if the backend fetches from S3 and forwards it, the file is downloaded twice and bottlenecks the backend.
optionExplanations: 后端只负责鉴权和签发 URL，字节传输交给对象存储直接服务客户端，后端不再是瓶颈。
全量代理意味着每个下载请求都要经过后端，大文件流量很快就能把应用服务器压垮。
把字节复制进数据库列既拖慢查询又浪费昂贵的关系型存储空间。
要求终端用户装数据库客户端既不现实，也把访问控制的边界完全打开了。
optionExplanations_en: Auth and signing are all it does on the backend; the actual bytes are served straight from blob storage, so it stops being the bottleneck.
Proxying every download through the backend means large-file traffic can overwhelm the app servers fast.
Copying bytes into a database column both slows down queries and wastes expensive relational storage.
Requiring end users to install a database client is impractical and blows open the access-control boundary.

scenario: S3 bucket 位于单一区域，全球用户下载大文件时跨地域延迟和带宽成本高。
q: 最合适的下载加速方案是什么？
options: 所有用户请求都固定从源站跨洲下载文件
用 CDN 缓存文件并发放短期 signed URL
把这些大文件统一塞进 Redis 内存缓存里
发动所有用户之间互相转发彼此的文件
options_en: Every user request always fetches across continents from the origin.
Cache files at CDN edge nodes and issue short-lived signed URLs.
Stuff all these large files into a Redis in-memory cache.
Have every user relay files back and forth to each other.
why: CDN 把热门文件放到离用户近的边缘节点，signed URL 仍保留访问控制。
why_en: A CDN caches files at edge locations near users while signed URLs keep access controlled.
whenOtherWins: 极冷、私密、只下载一次的文件不值得缓存，直接走 S3 signed URL 更省钱。
tradeoff: 边缘就近分发 vs 直连源站的简单与低成本

termDefinitions.meaning: 内容分发网络，把内容缓存到靠近用户的边缘节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN caches content on edge servers near users.

q_en: What is the best way to accelerate global downloads?
scenario_en: The S3 bucket is in one region, so global users downloading large files face high cross-region latency and bandwidth cost.
optionExplanations: 固定回源站等于放弃了地理就近这张牌，每个跨洲用户都要承受同样的高延迟。
热门文件被缓存到离用户近的边缘节点，短期 signed URL 又保住了访问控制，两头都不牺牲。
Redis 是单区域的内存缓存，不是分布在全球的分发网络，解决不了跨洲延迟。
让用户互相转发文件既没有访问控制，也没法保证内容没被篡改。
optionExplanations_en: Always hitting the origin gives up geographic proximity entirely — every cross-continent user eats the same high latency.
Popular files get cached at edge nodes near users, while URLs with a short lifetime still lock down who can fetch them — neither side gets sacrificed.
Redis is a single-region in-memory cache, not a globally distributed delivery network, so it can't fix cross-continent latency.
Having users relay files to each other leaves no way to restrict who gets it and no guarantee the content wasn't tampered with.

q: CDN 下载方案的主要成本问题是什么？
options: 这个 CDN 网络完全没办法缓存任何一个文件
用了 CDN 之后所有下载反而全部变慢
CDN 按流量计费，需要靠缓存策略控制成本
CDN 边缘节点会绕过所有签名校验机制
options_en: This CDN network cannot cache any files at all.
Using a CDN actually makes every download slower.
CDNs are billed by traffic, so cache policy controls cost.
CDN edge nodes bypass every signature check.
why: 不是所有文件都值得长期缓存在边缘，尤其是很少访问的私有文件；缓存策略决定成本与新鲜度。
why_en: Not every file deserves long-lived edge caching, especially rarely accessed private files, so cache policy controls cost.
q_en: What cost issue comes with using a CDN for Dropbox downloads?
optionExplanations: 缓存内容正是 CDN 存在的意义，这个说法直接否定了它的核心功能。
CDN 的目的就是加速分发，说它让下载变慢是反过来了。
CDN 按流量计费，靠缓存策略控制成本，哪些文件该留、该失效直接决定账单。
signed URL 本就配合 CDN 一起设计的访问控制手段，不会被边缘节点绕开。
optionExplanations_en: Caching content is the entire point of a CDN — this claim contradicts its core function.
A CDN exists to speed up delivery; saying it slows downloads down gets it backwards.
Edge caching is billed by traffic, so which files stay cached versus lapse quickly directly drives the bill.
Signed URLs are designed to work together with a CDN as the access-control layer, not something edge nodes skip.
scenario: Dropbox 用 CDN 加速下载，但大量私有文件一年只被访问一两次，边缘流量按 GB 计费。
scenario_en: Dropbox fronts downloads with a CDN, but many private files are read once or twice a year and edge traffic is billed per GB.

q: 把 sharelist 直接放在 FileMetadata 中的主要查询问题是什么？
options: 下载单个文件时反而没法检查访问权限
这个字段没法存储 uploadedBy 上传者信息
这时候没法保存文件的大小字段
查看“分享给我”的文件可能要扫描全部文件的 sharelist
options_en: Downloading a single file can no longer check access permission.
This field cannot store the uploadedBy uploader information.
The file size field cannot be saved at this point.
Listing files shared with me may require scanning every file's sharelist.
why: sharelist 放在 metadata 里对单文件鉴权很方便，但反向查 user -> files 需要扫描很多文件。
why_en: A share list on each file's metadata is convenient for single-file checks but makes shared-with-me queries scan many files.
q_en: What query problem comes from storing sharelist inside FileMetadata?
optionExplanations: 单文件权限检查恰恰是 inline sharelist 最擅长的场景，这个说法说反了。
uploadedBy 是完全独立的字段，跟 sharelist 放在哪里没有任何关系。
文件大小的存储方式跟分享列表设计是两件不相关的事。
反过来查“谁分享给了我”时，没有反向索引就只能把每个文件的 sharelist 都翻一遍。
optionExplanations_en: Single-file permission checks are exactly what an inline share list is good at — this gets it backwards.
uploadedBy is a completely separate field, unrelated to where the share list lives.
How file size is stored has nothing to do with the sharing list design.
Answering 'what's shared with me' without a reverse index means checking every file's sharing field one at a time.
scenario: Dropbox 要渲染「分享给我」页面：用户 A 想一次列出所有别人分享给他的文件。
scenario_en: Dropbox needs to render the shared-with-me page, where one user wants every file other people have shared with them.

scenario: 用户打开页面时需要快速看到所有别人分享给自己的文件，不能扫描全量 FileMetadata。
q: 更合适的数据模型是什么？
options: 只在每个 FileMetadata 里放一份 sharelist 字段
每次请求都在线扫描一遍所有文件
SharedFiles 表：userId 分区键，fileId 排序键
让客户端自己维护一张全局权限表
options_en: Keep only a sharelist field inside each FileMetadata.
Scan through every file online on each request.
A SharedFiles table: userId as partition key, fileId as sort key.
Let the client maintain its own global permissions table.
why: SharedFiles 直接建模 user -> shared file 的反向关系，查询某用户被分享的文件很快，也免去双写同步。
why_en: A SharedFiles table models the user-to-shared-file relationship directly, making shared-with-me lookups fast without a dual-write sync problem.
whenOtherWins: 分享功能很少用、只需单文件鉴权时，metadata 内 sharelist 更简单。
tradeoff: 规范化反向表的查询效率 vs 内联 sharelist 的实现简单

termDefinitions.meaning: DynamoDB 用来决定数据分布和主查询路径的主键字段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A partition key is the DynamoDB key field that determines data distribution and the primary query path.

diagram:
flowchart LR
User[User] --> Share[(SharedFiles)]
Share --> File[File metadata]
Owner[Owner] --> File
File --> Blob[(Blob object)]
q_en: What data model best supports the shared-with-me view?
scenario_en: The shared-with-me page must list all files shared with a user quickly, without scanning every FileMetadata record.
optionExplanations: inline sharelist 只支持正向查“这个文件分享给了谁”，反过来查用户拿到了哪些分享还是得全表扫。
每次请求都在线扫描全部文件，请求量一大直接打垮数据库，完全不现实。
查询模式是“按 user 反查分享给我的文件”，userId 分区、fileId 排序正好一次命中。
权限判断这种敏感逻辑交给客户端维护，既没法保证安全也没法保证跟服务端一致。
optionExplanations_en: An inline share list only answers 'who was this file shared with' — reversing it to 'what's shared with me' still means scanning everything.
Scanning every file on every request would crater the database the moment traffic grows — not realistic.
The query pattern is 'files shared with a user', so partitioning by userId with fileId as the sort key answers it in one lookup.
Letting the client maintain permission logic is neither secure nor guaranteed to match the server's state.

scenario: 需要在 DynamoDB 中查询某个用户收到的所有分享，并允许一个用户拥有多条 shared file 记录。
q: 哪种主键设计最贴合？
options: PK=fileId, 无 sort key
PK=userId, SK=fileId
PK=fileName
PK=mimeType
options_en: PK=fileId, with no sort key.
PK=userId, SK=fileId.
PK=fileName.
PK=mimeType.
codeSample:
| userId (PK) | fileId (SK) |
| user1       | fileId1     |
| user1       | fileId2     |
| user2       | fileId3     |
why: userId 分区能高效列出该用户收到的分享，fileId 排序键支持一个用户多条记录并保持唯一。
why_en: Partitioning by userId lists a user's shared files efficiently, while fileId as the sort key allows many records per user with uniqueness.
whenOtherWins: 如果主查询是 file -> users，需要改用 fileId 分区或额外反向索引。
tradeoff: 按 user 高效反查 vs 按 file 高效反查

termDefinitions.meaning: 决定数据分布和主要查询路径的主键字段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The partition key is the primary key field that determines data distribution and the main query path.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分区键相同时用于排序和唯一区分记录的辅助键。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The sort key orders and uniquely distinguishes records that share the same partition key.

q_en: Which DynamoDB key design best fits shared-with-me queries?
scenario_en: In DynamoDB, the system must list all files shared with a user and allow many shared-file records per user.
optionExplanations: 按 fileId 分区能查“这个文件被谁访问”，但答不了“这个用户收到了哪些分享”这个真正要问的问题。
userId 做分区键能一次列出用户收到的所有分享，fileId 做排序键又保证同一用户可以有多条记录。
fileName 既不是这里的查询维度，不同用户还可能撞同名，压根不能当主键用。
mimeType 只是文件类型，跟“谁能看这个文件”这种授权关系毫无关系。
optionExplanations_en: Keying on fileId answers 'who accessed this file', not the question actually being asked — what was shared with this user.
Partitioning the table by userId answers 'what's shared with this user' in one query, while a per-record fileId keeps duplicates from colliding.
fileName isn't even the query dimension here, and different users' files can share the same name, so it can't work as a key.
mimeType is just a file type — it has nothing to do with who's authorized to see the file.

q: inverse sharedFiles cache 相比规范化 SharedFiles 表的主要风险是什么？
options: 反向缓存根本没法加速 shared-with-me 查询
这种反向缓存结构不能存 fileId 字段
必须和 sharelist 保持同步，双写失败就会不一致
这种缓存结构只能用在下载场景里
options_en: This inverse cache cannot speed up shared-with-me queries at all.
This inverse cache structure cannot store the fileId field.
It must stay in sync with the sharelist; a partial write leaves them inconsistent.
This cache structure can only be used for the download scenario.
why: 反向 cache 查询快，但如果和 sharelist 不同步，权限和列表就会出错；正规化到同一张表能减少双写。
why_en: An inverse cache is fast to read but risks drifting from the file metadata share list unless both are updated together.
tradeoff: 反向缓存的读取速度 vs 单一数据源的一致性
q_en: What is the main risk of an inverse sharedFiles cache?
optionExplanations: 反向索引存在的理由就是加速这类查询，说它加速不了正好说反了。
fileId 完全可以作为反向缓存的值存进去，这不是它的限制。
两份数据分别写，只要有一次写失败或顺序错乱，缓存和 sharelist 就会各说各话。
这种反向索引能用在列表、鉴权等多个场景，不是专门为下载场景做的。
optionExplanations_en: The whole reason an inverse index exists is to speed up exactly this kind of query — this gets it backwards.
fileId can absolutely be stored as the cache's value; that's not a real limitation.
Writing to two places means one failed or out-of-order write leaves the cache and the share list disagreeing.
This kind of inverse index serves listing and authorization too, not just the download scenario.
scenario: Dropbox 为「分享给我」加了一份 user -> fileIds 的反向缓存，鉴权仍以文件上的 sharelist 为准。
scenario_en: Dropbox adds an inverse user-to-fileIds cache for shared-with-me, while authorization still reads the sharelist on the file.

q: Local -> Remote 同步中，客户端 sync agent 需要做哪些事？（多选）
options: 监听本地 Dropbox 文件夹的文件系统事件
检测变更后本地排队待上传文件
调用上传 API 把变更推到远端
把远端当作 source of truth 尽快更新
options_en: Watch the local Dropbox folder for filesystem events.
Queue changed files locally after detecting a change.
Call the upload API to push changes to the remote server.
Treat the remote server as the source of truth and update it quickly.
why: 本地变更先被 agent 捕捉并排队，再通过上传 API 推到远端；远端是 source of truth。
why_en: The sync agent watches local changes, queues them, pushes updates through the upload API, and treats the remote server as the source of truth.
q_en: What should the client sync agent do for local-to-remote sync? (Select all that apply)
optionExplanations: 文件系统事件监听是变化被感知的第一步——没有它，agent 根本不知道用户改了哪个文件。
本地排队是为了防抖和批处理，避免一个文件保存几次就触发几次网络请求。
调用上传 API 才是变化真正离开本机、进入系统的那一步。
把远端当唯一真相来源意味着本地永远只是一个副本，冲突发生时该以远端为准。
optionExplanations_en: Watching for filesystem events is the first step in noticing a change at all — without it, the agent has no idea a file was edited.
Queuing locally debounces and batches changes, so saving a file five times doesn't fire five separate network calls.
Invoking the upload endpoint is the step where a change actually leaves the machine and enters the system.
Treating the remote as authoritative means the local copy is just a mirror, and conflicts resolve toward the remote.
scenario: Dropbox 桌面客户端要在用户保存文件后几秒内把变更推到云端，而网络随时可能断。
scenario_en: The Dropbox desktop client must push a change to the cloud within seconds of the user saving, on a network that can drop at any time.

q: Dropbox 这个设计对同步冲突采用的简化策略是什么？
options: 人工合并每个字节
所有冲突都拒绝
强一致锁住全球文件
last write wins
options_en: Manually merge every byte.
Reject every conflicting write.
Lock the file globally for strong consistency.
Last write wins.
why: 版本控制被放到范围外，所以用 last write wins 简化冲突；真实产品通常保留旧块或用版本号，而不是直接覆盖。
why_en: The design simplifies conflicts with last-write-wins, since versioning is explicitly out of scope.
q_en: What simplified conflict strategy does this Dropbox design use?
optionExplanations: 逐字节人工合并没法自动化，也不可能在用户保存文件的那一刻实时完成。
拒绝所有冲突写入意味着用户改完文件保存不了，产品直接不能用。
给全球文件加强一致锁会让每次写入都要等全球确认，直接违背高可用目标。
版本控制被明确划出了范围，剩下能自动化的最简单策略就是谁最后写谁生效。
optionExplanations_en: Merging byte-by-byte can't be automated, and it certainly can't happen instantly the moment a user hits save.
Rejecting every conflicting write means users can't save their edits at all — the product wouldn't be usable.
A strong global lock on every file means every write waits for a global acknowledgment, fighting the availability goal directly.
With versioning off the table entirely, the simplest automatable rule left is that the last write simply wins.
scenario: Dropbox 面试把版本历史划到范围外：两台设备离线各改了同一个文件，然后同时上线。
scenario_en: Version history is out of scope for this Dropbox design, and two devices edit the same file offline then come back online together.

q: Remote -> Local 只用 polling（轮询）同步，缺点是什么？
options: 变更发现慢，且没有变更时也浪费带宽/请求
无法保证最终一致
必须持久连接
不能使用 since timestamp
options_en: Change detection is slow, and idle polls waste bandwidth and requests.
It cannot guarantee eventual consistency.
It requires a persistent connection.
It cannot use a since timestamp.
why: 轮询简单可靠，但实时性差；没有变化时的请求也是纯浪费。
why_en: Polling is simple and reliable but detects changes slowly, and idle polls waste requests when nothing changed.
tradeoff: 轮询的简单可靠 vs 推送的实时性
q_en: What is the drawback of polling-only remote-to-local sync?
optionExplanations: 固定周期才问一次，变化和被发现之间天然有时间差，空跑的请求也是纯浪费。
轮询照样能最终发现所有变化，只是慢，不是做不到最终一致。
轮询恰恰是短连接周期性请求，不需要保持连接常开。
since timestamp 过滤增量正是轮询最常见的实现方式，不存在用不了的问题。
optionExplanations_en: Asking on a fixed interval always leaves a gap between a change and its discovery, and every empty poll is pure waste.
Polling still eventually finds every change; it's just slow, not incapable of eventual consistency.
Polling is exactly a series of short periodic requests — it doesn't need a persistent connection.
Filtering by a since timestamp is the standard way polling works; nothing stops you from using it.
scenario: Dropbox 客户端每 30 秒轮询一次 /files/changes，而多数用户一天只改几次文件。
scenario_en: The Dropbox client polls /files/changes every 30 seconds, but most users only change a few files a day.

scenario: 客户端需要尽快知道远端文件变化，但 WebSocket/SSE 连接可能断开，消息也可能丢。
q: Dropbox 同步最稳妥的通知策略是什么？
options: 同步这件事完全只靠每小时轮询一次
单连接推送变更，靠周期性 polling 兜底漏掉的事件
给每一个文件单独开一条 WebSocket 连接
同步通知完全依赖发邮件来提醒用户
options_en: Sync relies entirely on polling once every hour.
One connection pushes changes, backed by periodic polling.
Open a separate WebSocket connection for every single file.
Sync notifications rely entirely on sending emails to users.
why: push 给近实时体验，周期性 GET /files/changes 捕捉断线期间漏掉的事件，两者互补。
why_en: Push delivers near-real-time updates while periodic polling catches anything missed during a dropped connection.
whenOtherWins: 极简单低频系统可以只轮询；真正实时协作编辑需要更强的实时协议。
tradeoff: 推送的实时性 vs 轮询的可靠兜底

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端和服务器之间保持打开的双向通信连接。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebSocket is a persistent, bidirectional connection between client and server.

termDefinitions.meaning: Server-Sent Events，服务器向客户端单向推送事件的机制。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SSE (Server-Sent Events) lets a server push a one-way stream of events to the client.

q_en: What notification strategy is safest for Dropbox sync?
scenario_en: Clients need to learn about remote file changes quickly, but WebSocket or SSE connections can disconnect and miss messages.
optionExplanations: 每小时才问一次，文件改了用户要等将近一小时才看到，同步体验完全不合格。
单连接推送变更覆盖大多数情况，轮询再补一刀，断线漏掉的变化也不会真丢。
给每个文件单独开一条 WebSocket，连接数直接跟文件数挂钩，服务器扛不住。
邮件的送达延迟以分钟甚至更久计，撑不起“近实时”这个目标。
optionExplanations_en: Checking only once an hour means a change can sit unseen for nearly an hour — nowhere near acceptable sync latency.
One push connection covers most updates, and a recurring poll sweeps up anything dropped mid-connection so it doesn't stay lost.
Opening a separate WebSocket per file ties connection count directly to file count, which no server can sustain.
Email delivery lags by minutes at best, nowhere close to a target of feeling instant.

q: 把 Remote -> Local 混合同步流程排成正确顺序：
steps: 客户端周期性调用 GET /files/changes?since={timestamp} 补漏
远端文件 metadata 发生 created/updated/deleted
服务器通过单条设备连接推送 change notification
客户端按通知拉取 metadata 或文件内容
如果推送连接断开，轮询仍能发现 missed changes
why: push 是快路径，polling 是可靠性兜底；两者都围绕 since timestamp 或 change cursor 收敛到一致。
why_en: Push is the fast path and periodic polling is the reliability fallback, both converging around a since-timestamp or change cursor.
diagram:
flowchart LR
Change[Remote change] --> Notify[Push notification]
Notify --> Agent[Sync agent]
Agent --> Delta[List changes]
Delta --> Download[Download updates]
Timer[Periodic poll] --> Delta
q_en: Put the hybrid remote-to-local sync flow in the right order.

q: Dropbox 最终高层设计中的关键组件有哪些？（多选）
options: File Service 负责 metadata 和 signed URL 生成
Metadata DB 存 FileMetadata 和 SharedFiles
S3 存原始文件字节
CDN 为下载缓存和加速
options_en: File Service handles metadata and generates signed URLs.
Metadata DB stores FileMetadata and SharedFiles.
S3 stores the raw file bytes.
CDN caches and accelerates downloads.
why: File Service 是控制面，S3/CDN 是数据面，Metadata DB 保存文件与分享关系。
why_en: The File Service is the control plane, S3 and the CDN are the data plane, and the metadata database holds files and sharing relationships.
q_en: Which components appear in the final Dropbox high-level design? (Select all that apply)
optionExplanations: 整个系统的控制面落在 File Service 上——鉴权、生成签名 URL 都在这里发生，但字节从不经过它。
文件记录和分享关系存在这张表里，是查询“我的文件”“分享给我的文件”的数据来源。
S3 是数据面的落脚点，真正的字节内容全部存在这里，跟控制面完全分开。
CDN 站在 S3 前面，把常访问的文件缓存到离用户更近的位置，减少跨区域下载延迟。
optionExplanations_en: Authorization and URL signing both happen inside this service, the one piece that never lets bytes pass through it.
The metadata DB stores file records and who-shared-what-with-whom, the data source behind pages like 'my files' and 'shared with me'.
S3 is where the bytes actually live, kept entirely separate from where auth and metadata are handled.
The CDN sits in front of S3, caching frequently accessed files closer to users to cut cross-region download latency.
scenario: Dropbox 最终架构要把控制面（元数据、鉴权、签名）和数据面（大文件字节）分开画。
scenario_en: The final Dropbox architecture has to separate the control plane — metadata, authorization, signing — from the data plane carrying the bytes.

q: 生成 presigned URL 时，File Service 需要先调用 S3 网络接口吗？
options: 必须先上传整个文件
必须让客户端发送 AWS secret
不需要；通常是用服务端云凭证本地做加密签名
必须扫描所有 metadata
options_en: Yes, it must first upload the entire file.
Yes, the client must send its AWS secret.
No; it typically signs locally with the service's own cloud credentials.
Yes, it must scan all metadata first.
why: 生成 presigned URL 是本地加密签名操作，用自己的凭证签名即可，不在大文件数据路径上。
why_en: Generating a presigned URL is a local cryptographic signing operation using the service's own credentials, not a network round trip to S3.
q_en: Does the File Service need to call S3 before generating a presigned URL?
optionExplanations: 上传整个文件和生成签名 URL 是两个独立的步骤，生成 URL 根本不需要文件已经存在。
让客户端拿到 AWS secret 等于泄露长期云凭证，是绝对不该发生的事。
签名 URL 本质是拿服务端自己的凭证对路径和过期时间做一次本地加密运算，不用打网络请求给 S3。
生成签名只需要对象路径和过期时间两个参数，跟扫描全部 metadata 没关系。
optionExplanations_en: Uploading the whole file and generating the signed URL are separate steps — signing doesn't require the file to already exist.
Giving the client an AWS secret leaks a long-lived cloud credential, which should never happen.
Signing a URL happens locally — the service applies its existing keys to the path and expiry, with no network hop out to S3 at all.
Signing only needs the object path and an expiry time, nothing to do with scanning all metadata.
scenario: Dropbox 每次上传前都要发一个 presigned URL，File Service 的 QPS 不该被 S3 往返拖住。
scenario_en: Dropbox mints a presigned URL before every upload, and the File Service throughput must not be gated on a round trip to S3.

q: 为什么 50GB 文件不适合单个 POST 上传？（多选）
options: 容易超过客户端/服务器超时
浏览器、Web 服务器或 API Gateway 可能有请求体大小限制
网络中断后必须从头再来
用户看不到细粒度进度
options_en: It easily exceeds client/server timeouts.
Browsers, web servers, or API gateways may cap request body size.
A dropped connection forces a restart from the beginning.
Users cannot see fine-grained progress.
why: 单请求大文件在超时、大小限制、恢复能力和进度体验上都很差。
why_en: A single huge POST risks timeouts, payload-size limits, restart-from-zero failures, and no progress visibility.
q_en: Why is a single POST a bad fit for a 50GB file? (Select all that apply)
optionExplanations: 客户端和服务器双方都有请求超时设置，几十分钟的单次传输很容易先撞上超时被掐断。
浏览器、网关、负载均衡器往往对单次请求体大小设了硬上限，50GB 大概率直接被拒。
网络一断，之前传的字节全部作废，用户得从零开始重新传一遍整个文件。
单个大请求要么完全没响应要么直接完成，中间没法展示“传到百分之几了”。
optionExplanations_en: Both client and server enforce request timeouts, and a transfer lasting tens of minutes easily gets cut off before it finishes.
Browsers, gateways, and load balancers usually cap request-body size, so a 50GB payload gets rejected outright.
A dropped connection throws away everything sent so far, forcing the user to retransmit the whole file from zero.
A single giant request is either silent or done — there's no way to show the user 'you're 40% through'.
scenario: Dropbox 用户从家庭 Wi-Fi 上传 50GB 视频，请求要穿过一个托管 API Gateway。
scenario_en: A Dropbox user uploads a 50GB video over home Wi-Fi, and the request has to pass through a managed API Gateway.

scenario: 面试里算了一笔账：50GB 文件在 100Mbps 连接上要传约 4000 秒（约 1.11 小时）。
q: 这个耗时估算最能支持哪个产品决策？
options: 应该把带宽限制成 10Mbps 以便计费
上传接口不需要任何超时设置
必须提供进度指示和断点续传，避免用户空等一小时
可以要求用户全程不关闭浏览器且不能中断
options_en: Bandwidth should be capped at 10Mbps for billing purposes.
The upload endpoint needs no timeout settings at all.
Provide progress indication and resumable upload; users shouldn't wait an hour blind.
Require users to keep the browser open the entire time without interruption.
why: 近 1 小时且中途不能中断的体验不可接受，这直接推动分块、进度条和断点续传设计。
why_en: Nearly an hour with no way to pause makes the experience unacceptable, which is exactly why chunking, progress, and resumable upload are needed.
q_en: What product decision does this upload-time estimate support?
scenario_en: The interview estimate says a 50GB file over a 100Mbps connection takes about 4,000 seconds, or roughly 1.11 hours.
optionExplanations: 带宽限速是计费策略问题，跟这道题在算的“用户要等多久”完全是两个维度。
耗时越长反而越需要合理的超时设置来及时发现连接已经死掉，不是不需要。
近一小时的等待，中途还不能中断，这种体验逼着设计必须给出进度反馈和断点续传。
要求用户全程盯着浏览器不能动，这既不现实也没解决耗时长本身的问题。
optionExplanations_en: Capping bandwidth is a billing decision, a totally different axis from the wait time this estimate is actually about.
A longer transfer needs a sensible timeout even more, so a dead connection gets noticed — not less.
A wait that long, unable to pause partway through, is unacceptable — exactly why the design needs a progress bar and the ability to resume.
Requiring the browser to stay open the whole time is unrealistic and doesn't solve the underlying long-wait problem.

scenario: 面试里提到：Amazon API Gateway 这类托管入口的请求体上限约 10MB，远小于 50GB 文件。
q: 这个限制说明了什么设计约束？
options: 干脆把 API Gateway 这一层整个去掉
50GB 文件绝不能塞进单个 API Gateway 请求
数据库的连接数需要相应调大十倍
CDN 的缓存命中率会因此明显下降
options_en: Just remove the API Gateway layer entirely.
A 50GB file can never fit through a single API-Gateway request.
Database connection limits need to be increased tenfold.
CDN cache hit rate will drop noticeably because of this.
why: 50GB ÷ 10MB = 5120 次请求，网关按单请求体量收费也扛不住；大文件字节必须绕开网关直传 S3。
why_en: A 50GB file is 5120 gateway-sized requests, so the bytes have to bypass the gateway and go straight to S3.
q_en: What design constraint does this API Gateway limit reveal?
scenario_en: Managed entry points like Amazon API Gateway have payload limits around 10MB, far below a 50GB file.
optionExplanations: 网关本身还要处理鉴权、限流等一堆其他请求，不能因为一个大文件场景就拆掉整层。
10MB 的硬上限意味着字节根本进不了网关这条路，大文件必须走直传对象存储绕开它。
数据库连接数跟网关的请求体大小限制是两个不相关的资源维度。
CDN 命中率取决于缓存策略和访问模式，跟网关的请求体大小限制没有因果关系。
optionExplanations_en: The gateway still handles auth, rate limiting, and everything else — you can't tear down the whole layer over one large-file scenario.
A hard 10MB cap means the bytes can never fit through the gateway at all, so a large file has to skip it and land directly in blob storage.
Database connection limits are an unrelated resource dimension from the gateway's payload-size cap.
CDN hit rate depends on cache policy and access patterns, not on the gateway's payload-size limit.

scenario: 要上传 50GB 文件，用户需要看到进度，断网或关浏览器后也能从已完成部分继续。
q: 应该采用什么策略？
options: 让服务端先收完整 50GB 文件再切块处理
直接禁止用户上传任何大文件
把整个文件塞进一个巨大的 JSON 字段里
客户端切成 5-10MB chunks，支持断点续传
options_en: Have the server receive the full 50GB file before chunking it.
Simply disallow users from uploading any large file.
Stuff the entire file into one giant JSON field.
The client uploads in 5-10MB chunks with resumable support.
why: chunking 必须发生在客户端，否则仍然要先上传完整文件到服务器。chunk 粒度让进度、并行和断点续传都可实现。
why_en: Chunking must happen on the client, otherwise the whole file still has to be sent first; chunk granularity enables progress, parallelism, and resumability.
whenOtherWins: 很小文件可以单次上传；大文件和不稳定网络应使用分块/Multipart。
tradeoff: 客户端分块的可恢复性 vs 单请求实现的简单
diagram:
flowchart LR
LargeFile[Large file] --> Split[Split chunks]
Split --> Upload[Parallel uploads]
Upload --> Blob[(Multipart storage)]
Blob --> Complete[Complete upload]
Complete --> Meta[(Metadata DB)]

termDefinitions.meaning: 把大对象拆成多个部分分别上传，再由存储服务合并的机制。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Multipart upload splits a large object into parts uploaded separately, then assembled by the storage service.

q_en: What upload strategy supports progress and resume for a 50GB file?
scenario_en: A 50GB upload needs progress feedback and must resume after a network drop or browser close.
optionExplanations: 服务端先收完整文件再切块，等于超时和体积限制这两个问题一个都没解决。
禁止大文件上传直接违背了产品最核心的需求，不是可选项。
JSON 字段是文本结构，塞不下 GB 级的二进制内容，这条路根本走不通。
分块这个动作必须发生在客户端才有意义——每块能独立重试、独立展示进度，断网后接着传。
optionExplanations_en: Having the server take in every byte first before chunking leaves both the timeout and the size-limit problem unsolved.
Banning large-file uploads directly violates the core product requirement — not an option.
A JSON field is text-structured and can't hold gigabytes of binary content — this path is a dead end.
Chunking only pays off when it is done client-side — each piece can retry independently, show its own progress, and resume after a drop.

q: 分块上传的 chunk 大小应该怎么理解？
text: chunk 大小不是死记数字：太大时{{失败重传成本高}}；太小时{{请求和元数据开销高}}；5-10MB 只是常见面试锚点。
why: 真正要记的是取舍：chunk 要够小，断线后不用重传整份大文件；也要够大，避免请求数、ETag 列表和进度状态爆炸。实际上下限看云厂商 multipart API。
why_en: The point is the tradeoff, not a magic number: chunks should be small enough for cheap retries and large enough to avoid excessive requests and metadata.
tradeoff: 失败重传成本 vs 请求/元数据开销

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端为了断点续传，把大文件切出来的一段字节。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A chunk is a byte range split from a large file so upload can resume after failure.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对象存储提供的分块上传能力；每个云厂商会规定 part 的最小、最大大小和数量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Multipart upload is an object-storage feature whose part size and count limits depend on the cloud provider.

q_en: How should you reason about chunk size for multipart upload?

q: 只让客户端 PATCH chunk 状态的安全风险是什么？
options: 恶意客户端可伪造 chunk 状态，造成数据不一致
这样一来客户端就没法正常显示上传进度
这个云存储 S3 就不会返回上传成功
metadata 这张表没法存储数组字段
options_en: A malicious client can forge chunk status, causing data inconsistency.
This means the client can no longer show upload progress properly.
This cloud storage, S3, would not return upload success.
The metadata table cannot store array fields.
why: 客户端状态可伪造，不能当最终真相；需要服务端用 S3 校验后再确认整体状态。
why_en: Client-reported status can be forged and cannot be trusted as ground truth without server-side verification against S3.

termDefinitions.meaning: S3 为对象或分片返回的校验值，用于确认内容是否匹配。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An ETag is a checksum S3 returns for an object or part, used to confirm the content matches.

q_en: What is the security risk of letting the client PATCH chunk status by itself?
optionExplanations: 客户端说的话不能直接当真——恶意客户端能谎报某个 chunk 已传完，带偏 metadata 和 S3 的实际状态。
进度展示照样能正常做，跟这里讨论的伪造风险是两件事。
这个风险跟 S3 会不会返回上传成功没有关系，S3 该怎么响应还是怎么响应。
数组字段的存储能力跟安全风险无关，metadata 表完全存得下。
optionExplanations_en: You can't take the client's word for it — a malicious client can simply lie about a chunk being done, drifting metadata away from what S3 actually has.
Progress display still works fine; that's unrelated to the forgery risk being discussed here.
This risk has nothing to do with whether S3 returns upload success — S3 responds the same either way.
Whether array fields can be stored has nothing to do with the security risk; the metadata table handles them fine.
scenario: Dropbox 分块上传时客户端 PATCH 上报每个 chunk 完成，服务端据此把文件标记为可下载。
scenario_en: During a chunked Dropbox upload the client PATCHes each chunk as done, and the server marks the file downloadable based on that.

scenario: 客户端上传每个 part 后拿到 ETag；后端需要确认这些 parts 确实存在于 S3 multipart upload 中。
q: 后端应如何验证 chunk 状态？
options: 后端完全信任客户端上报的 PATCH body
查 S3 ListParts 核对 part/ETag
只看客户端本地显示的那个上传进度条数值
仅凭上传的文件名判断上传状态
options_en: The backend fully trusts the client-reported PATCH body.
Call S3 ListParts to check the part and ETag.
Just look at the progress bar value shown on the client.
Judge upload status purely from the uploaded file name.
why: S3 multipart 的单个 part 不触发事件通知，ListParts 能列出已上传 part 及 ETag 供后端核对。
why_en: Individual multipart parts don't trigger event notifications, so ListParts lets the backend confirm what S3 actually received.
whenOtherWins: 如果存储提供可靠的逐 part webhook，可改用事件驱动校验。
tradeoff: 服务端校验的可信度 vs 信任客户端上报的简单
q_en: How should the backend verify uploaded chunk state?
scenario_en: After each uploaded part, the client receives an ETag; the backend must verify those parts really exist in the S3 multipart upload.
optionExplanations: 完全信任客户端上报的内容，相当于把校验这一步直接跳过了。
S3 单个 part 上传成功不会主动通知后端，得调 ListParts 才能问到真实已传的 part 和 ETag。
进度条只是前端展示出来的那个数字，不代表后端存储那边真的发生了什么。
文件名字段完全不携带任何分片上传的状态信息，没法用来判断。
optionExplanations_en: Fully trusting whatever the client reports means skipping verification entirely.
A successfully uploaded S3 part doesn't push a notification to the backend — only calling ListParts tells you which parts and ETags actually landed.
A progress bar is just a number rendered on the frontend; it says nothing about what storage actually has stored.
The file name field carries no part-upload state at all — it can't be used to judge this.

q: 文件 fingerprint 在断点续传/去重中解决哪些问题？（多选）
options: 判断同一内容的文件是否以前尝试上传过
找到已经上传过的 chunks
避免把普通文件名当唯一标识
替代 fileId 作为 metadata 主键
options_en: Determining whether content identical to this file was uploaded before.
Finding which chunks have already been uploaded.
Avoiding relying on the plain file name as a unique identifier.
Replacing fileId as the metadata primary key.
why: fingerprint 基于内容识别重复和续传状态；fileId（如 UUID）仍应是 metadata 的主键，fingerprint 只是辅助字段。
why_en: Content fingerprints identify duplicates and resume state by content, while the file record still needs its own unique ID such as a UUID.

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于文件内容计算出的哈希值，如 SHA-256，用于识别相同内容。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A fingerprint is a content hash, such as SHA-256, used to identify identical content.

q_en: What problems does a file fingerprint solve for resume and dedup? (Select all that apply)
optionExplanations: 内容相同就会算出相同的哈希，靠它就能判断这份文件是不是之前已经传过了。
把 fingerprint 算到 chunk 粒度，就能精确知道续传时哪几块已经在远端、哪几块还没传。
文件名可以随便改、也可能重名，只有基于内容算出来的指纹才是可靠的判重依据。
fingerprint 是内容标识，metadata 记录仍需要一个独立、稳定的主键（如 UUID），两者不能互相替代。
optionExplanations_en: Identical content hashes to the same fingerprint, which is exactly what tells you this file was already uploaded before.
Computing the fingerprint at chunk granularity pinpoints which chunks already made it to the remote side during a resume.
File names can be changed or duplicated, so a content-based fingerprint is the only reliable way to detect duplicates.
A fingerprint identifies content, not a record — the metadata row requires a separate, stable primary key like a UUID; one can't replace the other.
scenario: Dropbox 用户断网后要重传 50GB 文件，而公司里几十个人上传的是同一份安装包。
scenario_en: A Dropbox user has to resume a 50GB upload after a dropped connection, while dozens of coworkers upload the exact same installer.

q: 把大文件 multipart upload 流程排成正确顺序：
steps: 客户端用每个 part 的 presigned URL 上传 chunk，并回报 ETag
客户端计算整文件和每个 chunk 的 fingerprint
后端调用 CompleteMultipartUpload 让 S3 组装对象
后端 CreateMultipartUpload，保存 uploading metadata，并返回 uploadId 和各 part URL
后端用 ListParts 验证 chunks 后更新状态
why: 先识别内容和续传状态，再建 multipart session；所有 part 验证通过后才调用 CompleteMultipartUpload。
why_en: The flow fingerprints content first, opens a multipart session, uploads and verifies parts, then completes assembly.
diagram:
flowchart TD
Init[Create upload session] --> Urls[Get chunk URLs]
Urls --> Put[PUT chunks]
Put --> Verify[Backend verifies parts]
Verify --> Commit[Commit metadata]

termDefinitions.meaning: 把大对象拆成多个部分分别上传，再由存储服务合并的机制。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Multipart upload splits a large object into parts uploaded separately, then assembled by the storage service.

termDefinitions.meaning: S3 为对象或分片返回的校验值，用于确认内容是否匹配。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An ETag is a checksum S3 returns for an object or part, used to confirm the content matches.

q_en: Put the large-file multipart upload flow in the right order.

q: 为什么 multipart upload 不意味着下载也必须按原始 chunks 下载？
options: 这个云存储 S3 永远只保存成多个不可组合的 parts
CDN 网络完全没办法下载大文件
组装完成后是普通对象，下载靠 signed URL 或 Range
现在的浏览器完全没法处理 Range 请求
options_en: This cloud storage, S3, always keeps it as separate, unmergeable parts.
A CDN network cannot download large files at all.
Once assembled it is a normal object; downloads can use a signed URL or Range.
Modern browsers simply cannot handle Range requests.
why: multipart 是上传协议细节，完成后对象表现为一个普通对象；下载靠 HTTP Range 而不是知道原始 chunk 边界。
why_en: Multipart is only an upload-time detail; once complete, the object behaves like any normal object, and downloads can use HTTP Range requests.
tradeoff: 上传时的分片协议 vs 下载时的完整对象语义

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端只请求资源的某个字节区间，而不是整个文件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An HTTP Range request asks for only a byte range of a resource instead of the whole file.

q_en: Why does multipart upload not force downloads to use the original chunks?
optionExplanations: CompleteMultipartUpload 这一步存在的目的就是把各个 part 合并成一个完整对象。
CDN 对大对象的缓存和分发能力跟它是不是分片上传的没有关系。
组装完成后是普通对象，下载靠 signed URL 或 Range，不用管当初怎么分片。
HTTP Range 请求是浏览器和服务器早就原生支持的标准能力。
optionExplanations_en: CompleteMultipartUpload exists for exactly this reason — to merge the parts back into one full object.
A CDN's ability to cache and serve a large object has nothing to do with whether it was uploaded in parts.
Once assembled it's just an ordinary object — you can fetch it with a signed URL or by requesting a specific byte range, no knowledge of the original chunks needed.
Byte-range HTTP requests are a long-standing, natively supported capability in browsers and servers.
scenario: Dropbox 的 50GB 文件已用 multipart 上传完成，客户端只想拉中间某一段做预览。
scenario_en: A 50GB Dropbox file finished uploading via multipart, and the client only wants a slice from the middle to preview.

scenario: 文件只修改了一小段，跨设备同步时不希望重新上传/下载整个大文件。
q: 应该如何加速同步？
options: 总是重传整个文件
删除本地文件后重新下载
把变化写进 HTTP header
只同步发生变化的 chunks
options_en: Always retransmit the entire file.
Delete the local file and re-download it.
Write the change into an HTTP header.
Sync only the chunks that changed.
why: 分块除了帮上传恢复，也能让同步只传变化的块，小修改传输量大幅下降。
why_en: Chunking also enables syncing only the changed pieces, so a small edit transfers far fewer bytes than the whole file.
whenOtherWins: 小文件或变化遍布全文件时，整文件传输更简单且开销可接受。
tradeoff: 只传变化块的效率 vs 整文件传输的实现简单
q_en: How should Dropbox speed up sync after a small file edit?
scenario_en: Only a small part of a file changed, and cross-device sync should not upload or download the whole large file again.
optionExplanations: 每次改一点点就重传整个文件，传输量跟修改大小完全不成比例。
删掉本地文件重新下载，实际传输量和整文件重传没什么区别，只是换了个方向。
HTTP header 是用来传元信息的，装不下实际的文件内容变化。
只要能识别出哪些 chunk 真正变了，一次小修改就只需要传那几个 chunk，跟总大小脱钩。
optionExplanations_en: Sending every byte again for every tiny edit means transfer size has nothing to do with how much actually changed.
Deleting and re-downloading transfers roughly the same amount of data as a full retransmit — it just goes the other direction.
HTTP headers carry metadata, not actual file content changes — there's no room for that.
Once you can tell exactly which chunks changed, a tiny change only needs to send those few chunks, decoupled from total size.

q: 固定大小 chunk 在文件开头插入 1 字节会造成什么问题？
options: chunk 边界整体偏移，fingerprint 多数变化
插入字节之后只有第一个 chunk 会发生变化
这时候文件就没法再进行加密了
这时候 CDN 就没办法缓存这个文件了
options_en: Chunk boundaries all shift, and most fingerprints change too.
Only the first chunk changes after the byte is inserted.
The file can no longer be encrypted at this point.
A CDN can no longer cache this file at this point.
why: 固定边界对插入/删除很敏感，一次偏移会连锁改变后续所有块的哈希。
why_en: Fixed boundaries are sensitive to insertions; one shift cascades and changes the hash of every downstream chunk.

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于文件内容计算出的哈希值，用于识别相同内容。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A fingerprint is a content hash used to identify identical content.

q_en: What happens when one byte is inserted at the start of fixed-size chunks?
optionExplanations: 插入一个字节让后面内容整体后移一位，固定大小的切法只认字节偏移量，边界全部错位。
受影响的远不止第一块——插入点之后的每一块内容和哈希都会跟着变。
文件能不能加密是完全独立的功能，跟分块边界策略没有关系。
CDN 缓不缓存这个文件取决于访问模式和缓存策略，不取决于分块方式。
optionExplanations_en: Inserting one byte shifts everything after it by one position, and fixed-size boundaries only track byte offsets, so every later boundary moves.
Far more than the first chunk is affected — every chunk after the insertion point changes content and hash.
Whether a file can be encrypted is a completely separate feature, unrelated to chunk-boundary strategy.
Whether a CDN caches this file depends on access patterns and cache policy, not on how it was chunked.
scenario: Dropbox 用固定 4MB 分块做增量同步，用户在一个 1GB 文件的开头插入了 1 个字节。
scenario_en: Dropbox does delta sync with fixed 4MB chunks, and the user inserts a single byte at the very start of a 1GB file.

scenario: 希望小范围编辑只影响附近块，而不是让后面所有固定大小块都重新计算和同步。
q: 应采用哪种 chunk 边界策略？
options: 永远固定每 5MB 切一刀，边界从不改变
CDC：用 rolling hash 按内容决定边界
按照文件名字符串的长度来切块
按照上传用户的 ID 来决定切块方式
options_en: Always cut every fixed 5MB; the boundary never changes.
CDC: use a rolling hash to set boundaries by content.
Chunk based on the length of the file name string.
Chunk based on the uploading user's ID.
why: CDC 用内容模式决定边界，小插入通常只影响周围少数 chunk。
why_en: Content-defined chunking sets boundaries from content patterns, so a small edit usually affects only a few nearby chunks.
whenOtherWins: 只需要上传续传、不做 delta sync 时，固定大小分块更简单。
tradeoff: 内容边界的局部影响 vs 固定边界的实现简单
diagram:
flowchart LR
File[File bytes] --> Rolling[Rolling hash]
Rolling --> Boundary[Content boundaries]
Boundary --> Fingerprint[Chunk fingerprints]
Fingerprint --> Delta[Upload changed chunks]

termDefinitions.meaning: 随窗口滑动增量计算的哈希，用于在内容中快速定位分块边界。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A rolling hash is computed incrementally as a window slides over the data, used to quickly locate chunk boundaries by content.

q_en: Which chunk-boundary strategy keeps small edits local?
scenario_en: A small edit should only affect nearby chunks, not force every later fixed-size chunk to be recalculated and synced.
optionExplanations: 固定切法只看字节偏移，编辑点之后的每一刀都会跟着挪位，牵连范围完全不可控。
边界跟着内容模式走而不是固定字节数，插入或删除只影响附近少数几个 chunk。
文件名字符串长度跟文件内容毫无关系，按它切块纯属拍脑袋。
上传用户的 ID 是权限信息，跟数据本身该怎么切分是两个维度。
optionExplanations_en: A fixed cut only tracks byte offsets, so every boundary after the edit point shifts too — the blast radius is uncontrollable.
When boundaries follow what's actually in the data instead of a fixed byte count, an edit's impact stays limited to the chunks right around it.
File name length has nothing to do with file content — chunking on it would be arbitrary.
The uploading user's ID is authorization data, a different axis entirely from how the bytes should be split.

q: 提升上传、下载和同步速度的手段有哪些？（多选）
options: CDN 加速下载
chunks 并行上传和自适应 chunk 大小
只同步变化 chunks
对适合的文件客户端压缩后再上传
options_en: CDN accelerates downloads.
Parallel chunk upload with adaptive chunk size.
Sync only the changed chunks.
Compress suitable files on the client before uploading.
why: 下载靠就近边缘节点，上传靠并行分块，同步靠只传差异，压缩靠减少字节。
why_en: Downloads benefit from a nearby CDN edge, uploads from parallel chunking, sync from delta transfer, and suitable files from compression.
q_en: Which techniques improve upload, download, and sync speed? (Select all that apply)
optionExplanations: 下载慢的根源常常是物理距离，CDN 把内容挪到离用户更近的边缘节点直接压缩这段距离。
并行传多个 chunk 能把带宽用满，chunk 大小再跟着网络状况自适应，进一步榨出吞吐。
同步小修改时只传变化的部分，传输量跟改动大小挂钩，而不是跟文件总大小挂钩。
文本一类的文件客户端压缩后体积明显变小，传输时间跟着直接下降。
optionExplanations_en: Slow downloads often come down to physical distance, and a CDN cuts that distance by serving content from an edge node near the user.
Uploading multiple chunks in parallel saturates available bandwidth, and adapting chunk size to network conditions squeezes out more throughput.
Syncing a small edit by sending only the changed pieces ties transfer size to how much changed, not to the file's total size.
Compressing files like text on the client meaningfully shrinks their size, directly cutting transfer time.
scenario: Dropbox 用户抱怨跨洲下载慢、大文件上传久，而且改一点点就要重传整份文件。
scenario_en: Dropbox users complain that cross-continent downloads crawl, big uploads drag, and one small edit re-sends the whole file.

scenario: 客户端准备上传一个 5GB 文本文件，网络较慢；压缩时间可能小于节省的传输时间。
q: 是否应压缩？
options: 不应压缩任何文件
必须让后端下载后再压缩
客户端压缩后上传，下载后解压
先加密再压缩以提高压缩率
options_en: Never compress any file.
Have the backend download the file then compress it.
Compress on the client before uploading, decompress after downloading.
Encrypt first, then compress to raise the compression ratio.
why: 文本类文件压缩比高，客户端压缩省传输字节且不让后端进数据路径。
why_en: Text files compress well, so client-side compression saves transfer bytes without pulling the backend into the data path.
whenOtherWins: PNG、视频等已压缩媒体收益很小，压缩/解压时间可能不值得。
tradeoff: 压缩节省传输时间 vs 压缩/解压本身消耗的时间

termDefinitions.meaning: 常见的通用压缩算法，速度与压缩比各有取舍。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Gzip, Brotli, and Zstandard are common general-purpose compression algorithms with different speed/ratio tradeoffs.

q_en: Should Dropbox compress this upload?
scenario_en: The client is uploading a 5GB text file over a slow network, and compression time may be less than the transfer time saved.
optionExplanations: 文本类文件的压缩比通常很可观，一律不压缩等于白白浪费带宽。
后端先下载再压缩，意味着未压缩的完整文件已经先传了一遍，压缩收益全打了水漂。
客户端压缩后上传、下载后解压，省下实打实的传输字节，后端全程不碰这份数据。
先加密会把数据搅成接近随机的样子，之后再压缩基本找不到规律可压。
optionExplanations_en: Text files often compress substantially, so never compressing at all just wastes bandwidth for no reason.
If the backend downloads first and compresses after, the full uncompressed file already crossed the wire once — the savings are gone.
Compressing on the client before upload and decompressing after download cuts transferred bytes, and the backend never touches the raw data.
Encrypting first turns the data into something close to random, leaving compression almost nothing to work with afterward.

q: 为什么需要先压缩再加密？
options: 压缩会破坏所有加密
S3 不支持加密文件
CDN 只能服务未压缩文件
加密后数据近似随机，几乎压不动
options_en: Compression breaks all encryption.
S3 does not support encrypted files.
A CDN can only serve uncompressed files.
Encrypted data looks near-random, so it barely compresses.
why: 压缩依赖数据里的冗余模式，加密恰恰要消除这种模式，所以要先压缩再加密。
why_en: Compression relies on redundancy in the data, and encryption is designed to remove exactly that pattern, so compress before you encrypt.
tradeoff: 先压缩后加密的高压缩比 vs 顺序颠倒时几乎无压缩收益
q_en: Why should compression happen before encryption?
optionExplanations: 压缩本身不会破坏加密算法，真正的问题出在顺序上。
S3 完全能存储加密之后的对象，这不是它的限制。
CDN 对已压缩内容的缓存和分发没有任何障碍。
加密后数据近似随机，几乎压不动。
optionExplanations_en: Compression itself doesn't break the encryption algorithm — the real problem is ordering.
S3 fully supports storing encrypted objects; that's not a limitation.
A CDN has no trouble caching and serving already-compressed content.
Compression finds repeated patterns, while encryption exists specifically to erase those patterns into near-random noise — reverse the order and there's nothing left to compress.
scenario: Dropbox 客户端上传 1GB 日志前要同时做压缩和加密，目标是把上传字节数压到最低。
scenario_en: The Dropbox client both compresses and encrypts a 1GB log before upload, aiming to minimize the bytes actually sent.

q: Dropbox 文件安全应覆盖哪些基础措施？（多选）
options: HTTPS 加密传输
S3/server-side encryption at rest
基于 share table / ACL 的访问控制
短期 signed URL
options_en: HTTPS encrypts data in transit.
Server-side encryption at rest in S3.
Access control based on a share table / ACL.
Short-lived signed URLs.
why: 传输、静态存储、访问控制、临时令牌是文件安全的四个基础层。
why_en: File security layers encryption in transit, encryption at rest, ACL-based access control, and short-lived signed URLs.
q_en: Which baseline security measures should Dropbox file storage cover? (Select all that apply)
optionExplanations: HTTPS 挡住的是传输路径上的窃听——没有它，文件字节在公网上就是明文飞。
静态加密挡住的是存储介质本身被拿走或被越权访问的风险，跟传输安全是两道独立防线。
基于 share table/ACL 的访问控制决定“谁能看这个文件”，是权限把关，跟加不加密无关。
短期 signed URL 把泄露窗口压缩到分钟级，就算 URL 被转发出去也很快失效。
optionExplanations_en: HTTPS blocks eavesdropping on the wire — without it, file bytes fly across the public internet in plain text.
Encrypting stored data guards against the storage medium itself being taken or accessed without authorization, a separate line of defense from transport security.
ACL/share-table rules decide who's allowed to see the file at all, independent of whether it's encrypted.
Issuing a URL that expires quickly shrinks the exposure window to minutes, so even a forwarded URL goes stale fast.
scenario: Dropbox 的私有文件要走公网传输、落在第三方对象存储，并只让被分享者临时拿到下载入口。
scenario_en: Dropbox private files travel the public internet, land in third-party object storage, and only invited people may briefly get a download entry point.

q: signed URL 的安全局限是什么？
options: 它是 bearer token，拿到 URL 就能下载
这种签名 URL 完全没有办法设置过期时间
这种 URL 完全不能配合 CDN 一起使用
这种 URL 里必须包含用户的登录密码
options_en: It's a bearer token; whoever holds the URL can download it.
This signed URL has absolutely no way to set an expiration.
This kind of URL cannot be used together with a CDN at all.
This URL must contain the user's login password.
why: 短过期时间只能缩小泄露窗口，不能阻止持有者转发；更高安全场景可加 IP 绑定。
why_en: A short expiry only narrows the exposure window; it cannot stop a holder from forwarding the URL to someone else.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只要持有该凭证就能使用对应权限的令牌，不额外验证持有者身份。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A bearer token grants access to whoever holds it, without further verifying the holder's identity.

q_en: What is the security limitation of a signed URL?
optionExplanations: signed URL 本质是个 bearer token——过期前，谁拿到这串 URL 谁就能下载。
设置过期时间恰恰是 signed URL 最核心的机制，不是它做不到的事。
signed URL 配合 CDN 是非常常见的组合用法，不存在冲突。
签名本身就是凭证，URL 里不需要也不应该塞进用户密码。
optionExplanations_en: A signed URL is essentially a bearer token — anyone holding that URL can download until it lapses, since the server can't tell who's actually holding it.
Setting an expiration is the core mechanism of a signed URL, not something it fails to do.
Pairing a signed URL with a CDN is a common, well-supported combination — there's no conflict.
The signature itself is the credential; the URL shouldn't and doesn't need to carry a user password.
scenario: Dropbox 给下载者发了一个 15 分钟过期的 signed URL，对方把这个链接贴进了群聊。
scenario_en: Dropbox hands a downloader a signed URL that expires in 15 minutes, and they paste that link into a group chat.

q: 把 CDN signed URL 的验证流程排成正确顺序：
steps: CDN 收到请求后用公钥验证签名并检查过期/限制
服务端用私钥对 path、expiration 等生成签名 URL
授权用户拿到 signed URL
验证通过则 CDN 返回内容，否则拒绝
用户向 CDN 请求该 URL
why: 服务端用私钥签发短期访问权，CDN 在边缘验证签名和过期时间，无需每次回源问应用服务。
why_en: The server signs short-lived access with its private key, and the CDN verifies the signature and expiry at the edge without asking the origin every time.
diagram:
flowchart LR
Client[Client] --> App[File Service]
App --> Token[Signed URL]
Client --> CDN[CDN validates token]
CDN --> Blob[(Blob origin)]
q_en: Put the CDN signed-URL validation flow in the right order.

q: 把“大文件上传”这一 marquee 决策链排成正确顺序：
steps: 用 S3 multipart upload、per-part presigned URL 和 ETag/ListParts 验证
成本：metadata 和 object state 需要处理 uploading/complete/cleanup
需求：50GB 文件、进度条、断点续传、低后端带宽
选择客户端 chunking，避免服务端先收完整文件
用 fingerprint 支持续传和去重判断
why: 需求先排除单 POST，再把分块、指纹和 multipart 组合起来；代价是控制面状态机更复杂，但后端不再扛大对象流量。
why_en: The requirements rule out single-POST upload, then combine client chunking, fingerprints, and multipart upload, at the cost of a more complex control-plane state machine.
q_en: Put the large-file-upload decision chain in the right order.

q: Dropbox 这道题里，Senior 及以上候选人应主动深入哪些方向？（多选）
options: presigned URL / Blob Storage 直传
multipart upload、resumable upload 和 ETag 校验
CDN 下载、delta sync、content-defined chunking
把所有文件放进应用服务器本地磁盘
options_en: Presigned URLs and direct blob storage transfer.
Multipart upload, resumable upload, and ETag verification.
CDN downloads, delta sync, and content-defined chunking.
Storing all files on the application server's local disk.
why: 面试期望 Senior 快速过基础 API 和元数据模型，把时间花在大文件传输优化上。
why_en: Senior candidates are expected to move quickly through the basic API and data model, spending their time on large-file transfer optimizations.

flowchart LR
Client[Client Sync Agent] -->|metadata/auth| FileSvc[File Service]
FileSvc --> Meta[(Metadata DB)]
FileSvc -->|signed URL| Client
Client -->|upload/download bytes| S3[(S3 Blob Storage)]
S3 --> CDN[CDN]
